column1: # 2027-2029 (track T4, 11 Oct 2026): the fixed table as IFI prints it, in GMT all year (ifi_dublin_a.txt, identical to the local
# row's file but for the summer hour on every day), assigned to 2027, 2028 and 2029 dates (archive: ifi_dublin_gmt_<yyyy>.txt,
# derived; no 29 February is printed), the rest of the leap cycle, as ae-iacad.tsv's perpetual tables, each read on its own clock,
# UTC+00:00, so that each year's clock changes fall where Ireland's do. Computed with each year's own sun, 2027 was a minute
# early on 52 starts (Maghrib 37, Asr 14, Dhuhr 1) and a minute late on 29 ends, and 2028 worse: the method is now the fixed
# table it is (TimetableMethod.fixedTableYear = 2026, Europe.kt), every year computed as the year it was fitted on and held
# to the date's own sun (no sunrise after the sun's, no Maghrib before the minute after its sunset). So these rows are not
# held-out years (review of track T4): each compares the 2026 computation, moved, with the 2026 table re-dated; what they
# check is the move itself on each year's own clock, its clock-change days, and the date's own sun's bounds, a minute late
# where the sun has moved past the table (March 2028). Fit.
